label: second token z, after a first token from a fixed subset
explanation: Fires only at step 1 (second original token) when the input is z and the first token is one of a,c,d,e,f,g,h,i,j,l,n,o,r,t,x,y,0. The rule is deterministic on dev: precision 1.0 for each of these first tokens and 0 for the rest (b,k,m,p,q,s,u,v,w,z,1,2,3). The set looks arbitrary rather than a natural category. Magnitude depends on the first token: r gives max (0.79), letters like c/y/g/e/0 give about 0.7, l/t about 0.32, d about 0.12. It does not fire on z at any other position, on the copy-phase output of z, or on the delimiter, apart from one weak activation at step 17.

issues: None that matter. On test the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0 and mass recall 1.0 (9416 active, 9416 predicted). Misses on test found 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.
The dev profile matches the claims. All activation is at t=1 with in_tok z. There are 0 activations on the delimiter. The only stray activation is one copy-phase step at t=17 (out_tok 3).

The magnitude claims are only roughly supported: shares of activation mass by prev_tok are consistent with them. Counts are similar (~560-600) for c, y, g, e, 0, d, l and h, but mass is ~0.07 for c, y, g, e and 0, 0.030 for l and 0.012 for d. So d is weak and l is moderate, as claimed. Exact per-token magnitudes were not checked directly.
Minor: the label calls the first-token subset 'fixed', which is accurate but not very informative. The subset has no natural categorical description, and the explanation openly says so.
